title: Fernwheel Robotics — Q2 2026 Board Update
body:
Fernwheel Robotics — Quarterly Update, Q2 2026
Prepared by Iris Kwan, Founder & CEO. Distributed to the board ahead of the 21 July meeting.

Headline
Q2 was our strongest quarter since the Series A. We closed the quarter at $3.4M ARR, up from $2.6M at the end of Q1 (+31% QoQ). Net revenue retention held at 118%. Gross margin improved to 61% as we moved the last two pilot customers off the subsidised hardware bundle.

Commercial
The big story is the pipeline. Our new VP Sales, Sofia Lindqvist, started on 4 May and has already rebuilt the qualification process top to bottom. Sofia came to us after seven years running EMEA enterprise sales at a warehouse automation vendor, and it shows: pipeline coverage for H2 now sits at 3.8x, up from 1.9x when she arrived. The most significant open opportunity is Halloran Freight Group, a mid-market logistics operator with 14 distribution sites. Sofia and I presented to their operations leadership in June; they have confirmed a paid pilot at their Rotterdam hub starting September, with a potential rollout worth roughly $900K ARR if conversion targets are hit. I want to flag that Halloran will likely ask for uptime commitments beyond our standard SLA — we may bring this to the board if the delta is material.

Product & Engineering
We shipped v2.3 of the fleet controller with multi-bay routing, which was the main technical blocker for sites above ten picking cells. Two robotics engineers and one embedded firmware engineer joined in Q2; we are now 34 FTEs. Remaining priority hires for H2: a staff perception engineer and two customer deployment leads.

Finance & Runway
Marcus Delaney, our CFO, closed the quarter with $11.2M cash on hand and net burn of $780K/month, giving us just over 14 months of runway on the current plan. Marcus has also opened a conversation about a $4–5M venture debt facility to extend runway past the next fundraise window without further dilution. We have had two exploratory calls with Deepak Rao at Cormorant Partners, who led the debt facility for one of our Series A co-investors' portfolio companies last year. Terms discussed so far are indicative only (roughly 11% all-in with a 12-month interest-only period); Marcus will circulate a full comparison memo before the board meeting, including one alternative term sheet. No decision is requested at this stage — this is for discussion on 21 July.

Risks
1. Hardware lead times: our gripper supplier moved from 8 to 12 weeks; Marcus has priced a second-source qualification into the H2 budget.
2. Concentration: if Halloran converts, they would represent ~21% of ARR. Sofia is deliberately balancing the pipeline with three smaller mid-market deals to offset this.
3. Hiring: the staff perception engineer search is slow; we are widening it to remote-first candidates.

Asks for the board
- Feedback on the venture debt exploration before we go deeper with Cormorant Partners.
- Introductions to operations leaders at multi-site logistics groups in the Nordics — Maya, your network here has been invaluable before.

Looking forward to seeing everyone on the 21st.

— Iris

title: Fernwheel Robotics — Board Meeting Minutes, 21 July 2026
body:
FERNWHEEL ROBOTICS LTD
Minutes of the Meeting of the Board of Directors
Date: 21 July 2026, 14:00–16:00 BST. Held by video conference.

Present: Iris Kwan (Founder & CEO, Director), Maya Chen (Nordwind Ventures, Director), Jonas Berg (Nordwind Ventures, Observer). Also in attendance for items 2–4: Marcus Delaney (CFO) and Sofia Lindqvist (VP Sales), by invitation.

A quorum being present, Iris Kwan chaired the meeting and Jonas Berg agreed to take minutes.

1. Approval of prior minutes
The minutes of the 22 April 2026 meeting were approved as circulated. Unanimous.

2. CEO and financial report
Iris Kwan walked through the Q2 update previously distributed. Marcus Delaney presented the financial pack: $3.4M ARR, $11.2M cash, net burn $780K/month, ~14 months runway. Maya Chen asked whether the burn plan assumed the two H2 deployment-lead hires; Marcus confirmed it did, and that the staff perception engineer hire would add approximately $25K/month fully loaded from October. The board noted the report.

3. Commercial pipeline — Halloran Freight Group
Sofia Lindqvist presented the pipeline review. The board discussed the Halloran Freight Group opportunity at length. Sofia confirmed the Rotterdam pilot is contracted to begin the week of 7 September, with a conversion decision expected by mid-November. Maya Chen raised the customer-concentration risk (~21% of ARR on full rollout) and asked that the pilot contract not include exclusivity or MFN provisions; Iris confirmed none are contemplated, and agreed to have Elena Ruiz at Bright & Field review the master services agreement before signature given the non-standard uptime commitments Halloran has requested. ACTION: Iris to route the Halloran MSA to Elena Ruiz by 8 August.

4. Venture debt facility
Marcus Delaney presented a comparison memo covering two indicative proposals: (a) Cormorant Partners, via Deepak Rao, at approximately 11% all-in with a 12-month interest-only period and warrants for 0.35% fully diluted; and (b) an unnamed bank alternative at a lower headline rate but with a cash-covenant structure Marcus considered restrictive at the current burn profile. Jonas Berg noted that Nordwind has two portfolio companies with active Cormorant facilities and offered to gather reference feedback. After discussion, the board authorised management to negotiate a term sheet with Cormorant Partners up to $5.0M principal and warrant coverage not exceeding 0.40%, with any executed term sheet to return to the board for approval. Resolved unanimously. ACTION: Marcus to report back with a negotiated term sheet at or before the October meeting; Jonas to share reference feedback within two weeks.

5. Hiring and options
The board approved option grants to seven Q2 joiners as set out in Schedule A (on file), including the grant to Sofia Lindqvist per her offer letter, all at the current 409A-equivalent valuation. Resolved unanimously.

6. AOB
Maya Chen offered introductions to two Nordic logistics operators for the H2 pipeline. Next meeting: 20 October 2026, 14:00 BST, in person at Nordwind's London office.

There being no further business, the meeting closed at 15:52.

Minutes recorded by Jonas Berg. Approved by the Chair.
